title: Macquarie secures $1.45bn in unusual bond play
full_text:
Macquarie Group’s latest bond raising in the market has piqued interest among investors on the back of what has been described as an unusual tenor.
The Australian listed bank is raising $1.45bn of capital through the bond market and one of the offerings will be a 10-year floating rate note.
Market experts say such offerings are scarce because the market does not have a lot of appetite for them.
ANZ embarked on one about two months ago but was not met with overwhelming demand.
However, in Macquarie’s latest overall bond offering it attracted about $3bn worth of demand.
The issue was under way on Tuesday, with the National Australia Bank spearheading the deal as a book runner.
It was part of Macquarie’s move to secure regulated capital. Two bonds were at a 5.5-year tranche with a spread of 1.52 per cent. One of the bonds was fixed and another is floating.
The 10-year bond was 1.77 per cent above the three-month bank bill swap rate. It comes as the 10-year Treasury bond in the US rises to a 19-year high, sailing above 5 per cent in the past week, according to The Wall Street Journal.
As a result, it has pushed up the Australia 10-year government bond to over 5.3 per cent, which has acted as a deterrent to investors buying up stocks in the real estate sector for yield plays.
For the 2026 financial year, Macquarie generated a $4.85bn net profit, up 30 per cent on the previous corresponding financial year. Shares closed up 73c to $242.27.
